description: Reproducible performance profiling study comparing vLLM and nano-vllm using Triton's Proton profiler on 1x H100 80GB

userStories.title: Sanity check with Qwen3-0.6B
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to validate profiling scripts with a small model first so that I can catch issues before committing to expensive 32B runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Script scripts/profiling/sanity_check.sh profiles both nano-vllm and vLLM with Qwen3-0.6B on 1 GPU
Runs one profiling configuration (shadow+tree) for each framework
Output .hatchet files are loadable by proton-viewer without errors
Script completes in under 5 minutes
Script prints pass/fail summary indicating whether both frameworks produced valid profiles
Script activates venv via . .venv/bin/activate before running Python
Tests pass

userStories.title: Offline batch profiling scripts for nano-vllm
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want shell scripts that profile nano-vllm batch inference with Qwen3-32B so that I can reproduce the profiling runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Script scripts/profiling/nano_vllm_offline.sh profiles nano-vllm's bench.py with Qwen3-32B on 1 GPU
Script runs 4 profiling configurations: shadow+tree, shadow+trace, python+tree, python+trace
Each config outputs to a separate subdirectory under profiling_output/nano_vllm/offline/
Script uses --proton-hook triton to capture Triton kernel metadata
Workload parameters (batch size, sequence lengths) are configurable via script arguments
Script prints summary of output files on completion
Output .hatchet files are loadable by proton-viewer without errors
Script activates venv via . .venv/bin/activate before running Python
Tests pass

userStories.title: Offline batch profiling scripts for vLLM
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want shell scripts that profile vLLM batch inference with Qwen3-32B so that I can compare against nano-vllm.
acceptanceCriteria: Script scripts/profiling/vllm_offline.sh profiles vLLM offline inference with Qwen3-32B on 1 GPU
Uses vLLM's Proton profiler config via --profiler-config JSON
Runs same 4 profiling configurations as nano-vllm (shadow+tree, shadow+trace, python+tree, python+trace)
Each config outputs to a separate subdirectory under profiling_output/vllm/offline/
Matching workload to nano-vllm (same sequence count, input/output lengths, random seed)
Output .hatchet files are loadable by proton-viewer without errors
Script activates venv via . .venv/bin/activate before running Python
Tests pass

userStories.title: Online serving profiling scripts for nano-vllm
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to profile nano-vllm under online serving conditions so that I can compare scheduling and batching behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Script scripts/profiling/nano_vllm_online.sh profiles nano-vllm with simulated online requests
Uses periodic flushing mode to capture warmup phase and steady-state phase separately
Generates per-phase .part_N.hatchet files
Workload: sequential requests with varying prompt lengths to simulate online traffic
Output files are loadable by proton-viewer without errors
Script activates venv via . .venv/bin/activate before running Python
Tests pass

userStories.title: Online serving profiling scripts for vLLM
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to profile vLLM under online serving conditions with periodic flushing.

Captures warmup phase and steady-state phase separately
Matching workload to nano-vllm online script

Script activates venv via . .venv/bin/activate before running Python

userStories.title: Profile analysis with proton-viewer
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to analyze all captured profiles and extract key metrics so that I can compare the two frameworks quantitatively.
acceptanceCriteria: Script scripts/profiling/analyze_profiles.sh runs proton-viewer on all .hatchet files
Extracts and prints: top-10 kernels by time, total GPU time, kernel count
Compares vLLM vs nano-vllm side by side for each profiling mode
Saves proton-viewer output to profiling_output/analysis/ as text files
Chrome trace files (.chrome_trace) listed with instructions to open in Perfetto
For periodic flushing profiles, compares warmup phase vs steady-state phase
Script activates venv via . .venv/bin/activate before running Python
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005 (requires profile output files)

userStories.title: Summary report and reproducibility
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want a summary report with all findings and a master script to reproduce the entire study.
acceptanceCriteria: Master script scripts/profiling/run_all.sh runs all profiling scripts in sequence (sanity check first, then offline, online, analysis)
Summary report scripts/profiling/README.md documents: hardware setup, model, workload parameters, how to run, key findings
Report includes quantitative comparison table: throughput, top kernel times, scheduling overhead
Report includes observations about shadow vs python context differences
Report includes observations about tree vs trace format trade-offs
Report includes periodic flushing warmup vs steady-state comparison
All output directories and file naming conventions documented
